Short version: screens in the hour before bed delay sleep, since in a 2025 study of 1,200 kids aged 6 to 9 those kids fell asleep about 19 minutes later. The causes are light delaying melatonin, games and short videos that keep attention up, and screen time pushing out wind-down routines. The fix is a fixed screens-off time an hour before bed including weekends, devices charged outside the bedroom, and reading in the last half hour. Timing matters more than total screen time once it stays under two hours a day.
Action: send this summary back to you in a form you can paste to Hannah's group chat if you'd like.

A common rule of thumb is that a curve has flattened when the period-over-period drop shrinks to roughly a percentage point or less and stays there for several consecutive periods, so retention is approaching a floor. It also helps to check that the later cohorts flatten at a similar level and that the cohort sizes are big enough to trust. It's a convention, not a standard, so state your threshold in the writeup.

EFT is the umbrella term for electronic funds transfer between bank accounts in Canada, both credits (like direct deposit) and debits (like pre-authorized payments). ACH is the US network name, and in Canada the batch system underneath is run by Payments Canada, so people often use 'ACH' loosely to mean those batch bank transfers. Real-time payments are a separate rail. In short: EFT is the type of transfer, and ACH is the American name for the kind of batch network behind it.
Action: add a two line glossary entry to your payouts notes if that helps.
